newsitem.title: USA: UNIVERSAL SEES IMPROVED FY 1998 PROFITS.
newsitem.headline: UNIVERSAL SEES IMPROVED FY 1998 PROFITS.

text.p: Universal Corp said Thursday that a larger flue-cured tobacco crop anticipated in the U.S. should enable it to buy and process larger leaf volumes and improve profitability for its 1998 fiscal year.

Henry Harrell, chairman and chief executive officer, said Universal was also optimistic about the prospects for its new partnership with Socotab Leaf Tobacco Co Inc, in which the oriental leaf tobacco businesses of the two will be combined.
He said the deal is subect to approval of a definitive agreement by the boards of both companies and the transaction is expected to be completed within 90 days.
He said the partnership will be the world's leading oriental leaf merchant with revenues in excess of $300 million.

For its fiscal year ended June 30, Universal said its earnings rose 40 percent to $100.9 million or $2.88 per share, compared with net income last year. Gross revenues increased by 15 percent to $4.1 billion, it said.

Fourth quarter results were sharply higher than the same period last year, with net income for the latest quarter at $21.8 million or $0.63 per share, it said. That compares with $16.2 million or $0.46 per share last year or an increase of approximately 35 percent, it said.
